cards.b: No new substance is formed; usually easily reversible (e.g. melting, dissolving).
New substances are formed; usually difficult to reverse; often with energy change, gas, colour change or precipitate.
A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen at the same time.
Loss of electrons; oxidation number increases.
Gain of electrons; oxidation number decreases.
Oxidation Is Loss of electrons; Reduction Is Gain of electrons.
CO is oxidised (gains oxygen to form CO₂). Fe₂O₃ is reduced (loses oxygen).

cards.f: In Mg + CuO → MgO + Cu, what is oxidised and reduced?
cards.b: Mg is oxidised (gains O); CuO is reduced (loses O).

cards.f: What does the Roman numeral in iron(III) mean?
cards.b: The oxidation number of the ion: Fe³⁺ has charge 3+.

cards.f: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu: which is oxidised?
cards.b: Zinc: it loses 2 electrons. Cu²⁺ gains 2 electrons and is reduced.

cards.f: Test for water using cobalt(II) chloride
cards.b: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride turns from blue to pink.

cards.f: Test for water using copper(II) sulfate
cards.b: Anhydrous copper(II) sulfate turns from white to blue.

cards.f: Does the water test show the water is pure?
cards.b: No. It only shows water is present. Pure water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C.

short.q: State the difference between a physical change and a chemical change. [2]
short.model: In a physical change no new substance forms and it is easily reversed; in a chemical change a new substance forms.

short.q: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O identify the substance oxidised and the substance reduced, with a reason for each. [4]
short.model: H₂ is oxidised because it gains oxygen; CuO is reduced because it loses oxygen.

short.q: Explain, in terms of electrons, why Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu is a redox reaction. [3]
short.model: Zinc loses electrons (oxidation) and copper ions gain electrons (reduction) at the same time.

short.q: Describe a chemical test for water and a way to show the water is pure. [3]
short.model: Anhydrous copper(II) sulfate turns white to blue. Pure water has a boiling point of exactly 100 °C (melting point 0 °C).
points: anhydrous copper(II) sulfate white to blue

short.q: Name the ion Fe³⁺ and explain what the (III) shows. [2]
short.model: Iron(III); the number in brackets is the charge/oxidation number of the iron ion.
